source_checks.note: California's chaptered SB 53 supports a 10^26-FLOP frontier-model threshold and incident reporting within 15 days, with 24-hour disclosure for an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury. This is the timing the essay incorrectly applies to both California and New York.

New York's official amended RAISE text and action history show enactment as Chapter 96 on March 27, 2026 and require ordinary critical-safety-incident reporting within 72 hours, with 24-hour disclosure for imminent death or serious physical injury. The essay's shared 'within fifteen days' statement is therefore materially wrong for New York.

The FTC docket supports that the suppression-of-accuracy statement is proposed and open for comment, not final, and that its theory applies Section 5 deception to undisclosed output steering. This discharges the article's fetch-blocked FTC obligation but does not cure the state-law timing error.
The Federal Register public-inspection PDF confirms the proposed statement's text, docket, and state-law-conflict theory.

The Colorado Attorney General's official AI page supports that SB26-189 was signed in May 2026, repealed and reenacted the prior AI Act into a disclosure-centered regime, and is scheduled for January 1, 2027. This discharges the article's Colorado fetch obligation.
Executive Order 14365 supports the AI Litigation Task Force, Commerce review of state laws, grant/funding pressure, FTC direction, and proposed federal preemption framework described by the essay.
The White House document is legislative recommendations rather than enacted law and supports the article's quoted opposition to state regulation and a new federal AI rulemaking body.
The January 13, 2026 BIS release supports case-by-case review for H200, MI325X, and similar exports subject to US-capacity protection, purchaser compliance procedures, and independent US testing.
The Council's final-adoption release supports December 2, 2027 and August 2, 2028 high-risk-system dates and does not indicate a comparable deferral of the general-purpose-AI chapter.
The official Chinese national-standard record supports GB 45438-2025's status and effective labeling-regime provenance, discharging the article's stated labeling-measure fetch obligation.
The House discussion draft supplies the previously unfetched bill text and confirms that it is a proposal rather than enacted law.

hold_reasons: The article reports one shared incident-reporting window for California and New York: 15 days, or 24 hours if imminent. California uses 15 days, but New York's enacted amended RAISE Act uses 72 hours for ordinary critical safety incidents.
The error appears in the paragraph presented as the factual organizing claim of the American section, so it cannot be treated as a harmless source-note discrepancy.
unresolved_obligations: Correct the state-by-state incident-reporting timelines and bind each figure to its own enacted text before publication.
